title: TrailGenic Sleep Science Endurance Dataset

canonical_alignment.data_window: Historical sleep observations through Hike 31; not recomputed through Hike 34.
canonical_alignment.claim_boundary: Sleep and HRV observations do not validate a recovery governor, causal recovery closure, readiness score, or fatigue diagnosis.

description: Sleep-recovery dataset updated to 30 independent pre-hike recovery sequences and Western Altitude Block recovery archetypes.

sequence_counts.overlap_rule: Manitou overlaps the Elbert recovery window and is not counted as a separate sleep sequence.

structured_terms.recovery_closure: Restoration confirmed by architecture and autonomic direction, not duration alone.
structured_terms.recovery_demand_sleep: Long sleep opportunity with persistent low HRV, elevated RHR, stress, fragmentation, or compressed REM.
structured_terms.split_recovery_pattern: Autonomic markers may recover before REM or total sleep architecture.
structured_terms.recovery_governor: Retired causal framing. Completion and post-effort observations should be reported separately without asserting a validated physiological subsystem.

recovery_archetypes.mount_elbert: Severe strain followed by successful recovery closure.

records.mechanism: Sleep duration is recovery opportunity; architecture and autonomic direction reveal whether restoration occurred.
physiological_response: Elbert: severe Day-1 strain, successful Day-2 closure.
Pikes: successful performance with descriptive post-effort sleep and autonomic observations.
Wheeler: descriptive Day-2 change after compressed stacking; accumulated fatigue was not established as the mechanism.
adaptation_outcomes: Normal cadence usually restored; compressed stacking exposed the boundary.
